changelog:
- Major update: refocused on step-by-step setup and essentials for Awareness memory layer, simplifying instructions and clarifying scope.
- Updated description to guide users when persistent, cross-session AI memory is needed, especially for Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, or any MCP client.
- Removed all Bash and node script instructions, now providing unified MCP commands (awareness_init, awareness_recall, awareness_record, awareness_lookup).
- Added a one-command quickstart (npx @awareness.market/setup) and guidance on auto-injecting memory into agent workflows.
- Detailed features such as conflict detection, workflow rules injection, and benchmarks.
- Specified when not to use this skill (not an agent runtime, not for general RAG or agent marketplaces).
summary: Use when the user wants persistent cross-session memory for their AI agents — "make Claude Code remember my project", "让 AI 记住上下文", memory for Cursor/Windsurf/any MCP client, or when an agent keeps forgetting context between sessions. Gives step-by-step instructions for installing the Awareness memory layer (npx @awareness.market/setup) and using its MCP tools (awareness_init, awareness_recall, awareness_record, awareness_lookup). Works fully local-first with no account.
